name: fricas
why: An advanced open-source computer algebra system, a serious mathematical environment you can dig into for days.

brief.what_it_is: FriCAS is a general-purpose computer algebra system: a free, open-source environment for doing symbolic and exact mathematics. The homepage calls it an advanced computer algebra system and gives version 1.4.0. The README says its algebra library is one of the largest and most advanced free general-purpose CAS libraries, written in the strongly typed Spad language. The executables are efricas and fricas. I did not see the input and output formats in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the basic goal is to create a free, advanced, world-class CAS. FriCAS forked from Axiom in 2007 and is meant to be a foundation others can build on.
brief.how_it_works: The algebra library is written in Spad, a high-level, strongly typed language, which the README says lets mathematical algorithms be expressed naturally and makes the system easier to understand and extend. Compared with Axiom, the README says FriCAS was significantly restructured, is more portable, fixes several defects, and removed large unused parts without removing functionality.
brief.install_notes: The README says installation instructions are in an INSTALL file in the repository, which I did not fetch. Beyond that I saw no details on runtimes, accounts, or first-run steps. The homepage has an Installation Guide section, which I did not follow.
brief.standout: It is a long-lived fork of Axiom with a strongly typed, purpose-built language (Spad) under the algebra library, so the mathematics is written in a typed language rather than bolted on. The README also claims it is one of the largest free general-purpose CAS libraries.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is thin. The homepage says FriCAS 1.4.0 and copyright 2007-2026, and the README lists active development goals. I did not see a last-release date or last-commit date, so I could not confirm the timing.
brief.caveats: I saw no platform list or build notes in the pages I read, and I did not fetch the INSTALL file, so build difficulty is unknown. The homepage was reachable, but its contents are mostly a table of contents and links. The README gives no usage examples, so the Help and Examples sections were not checked. The homepage is licensed under a modified BSD license.
quotes: FriCAS is a general purpose computer algebra system (CAS).
The basic goal of FriCAS is to create a free advanced world-class CAS.
fetch_log: https://fricas.github.io: worked. Sphinx-style homepage with FriCAS 1.4.0 heading, a short description, and a table of contents. It has no commands or install steps.

https://github.com/fricas/fricas: worked. Returned the README, which points to an INSTALL file and the homepage for documentation. I did not follow the INSTALL file, the Installation Guide, or the Examples sections.

judge.reason: FriCAS is an unusual, extensible computer algebra system whose Spad language encodes sophisticated algebraic structures, making it a worthwhile rabbit hole beyond ordinary symbolic math.

entry.title: FriCAS
entry.tldr: A free computer algebra system for exact, symbolic mathematics, forked from Axiom, with its algebra library written in a strongly typed language called Spad.
entry.deeper_look:
FriCAS is a general-purpose computer algebra system. It is meant for symbolic and exact mathematics rather than floating-point number crunching. The project describes its basic goal as "to create a free advanced world-class CAS." Its README says its algebra library is one of the largest and most advanced among free general-purpose systems.

The idea underneath it is that the mathematics lives in a typed language. The algebra library is written in Spad, a high-level, strongly typed language. The README says this lets mathematical algorithms be expressed naturally and makes the system easier to understand and extend. Most computer algebra tools grow out of an untyped scripting layer. Here the types are part of how the math is described.

FriCAS forked from Axiom in 2007. According to the README, it has since been significantly restructured, made more portable, had several defects fixed, and had large unused parts removed without removing functionality. It is meant as a foundation others can build on. Axiom is a long-running system with deep academic roots, so this is a way into that lineage.

The brief did not cover the input syntax or example sessions. The homepage has Help and Examples sections to start from.
entry.install:
brew install fricas
# installs the fricas and efricas executables; depends on sbcl, gmp and some X11 libraries

Shows the options for the second executable, efricas.

entry.whats_unique: It is a long-lived fork of Axiom whose algebra library is written in Spad, a purpose-built, strongly typed language, so the mathematics is expressed in types rather than bolted onto a scripting layer.
entry.caveats: The pages read showed no usage examples, and the last-release date is unconfirmed, so expect to learn the syntax from the project's own documentation.
